title: Soil and cherry bacterial communities predict flavor on coffee farms
one_line: A farm-scale survey linking soil and coffee cherry bacterial community composition to sensory cup-quality scores, reporting that microbiome profiles are associated with (and predictive of) coffee flavor outcomes.
key_claims: Bacterial community composition differs between soil and coffee cherry compartments on working farms.
Variation in cherry- and soil-associated bacterial taxa is associated with differences in sensory flavor/cup-quality scores.
Microbiome features carry enough signal to predict flavor-related outcomes above baseline, per the authors' modeling.
Farm/site identity and environment structure the microbial communities that accompany flavor differences.
limitations: Observational survey design; associations between microbiome and flavor do not establish that microbes cause flavor differences.
Sensory scores are subjective panel outputs and may confound with agronomic, genetic, and processing variables not fully controlled.
Numeric effect sizes, sample counts and model accuracies were not available in the material supplied for this card.
Findings are tied to the sampled farms/regions and may not generalize to other origins or processing methods.
open_questions: Do controlled inoculation or microbiome-manipulation trials change cup scores in otherwise identical lots?
Does the predictive model hold on held-out farms, seasons, and origins?
Which specific taxa or metabolic pathways generate the flavor-active compounds, versus merely co-occurring with them?
